```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(tmap)
```

Load the data:

```{r}
cre_sf <- st_read("../data/processed/londonCRE.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r}
nrow(cre_sf)
```

Clusters in space:

```{r}
cre_projected <- st_transform(cre_sf, 3857)
london <- get_tiles(cre_projected, provider="CartoDB.PositronNoLabels", zoom=11)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggspatial) 

value_plot <- ggplot(data = cre_projected %>% filter(Volatility > 0)) +
  layer_spatial(london) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(color = Value), 
    size = 0.8,
    alpha=0.7,
    stroke = 0
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    option = "viridis",
    name = NULL,
    direction = 1,
    trans = "log10"
  ) +
  theme_void() + 
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.93, 0.08),
    legend.justification = c("right", "bottom"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(value_plot)
```

```{r}
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Build the plot with EPSG:3857 meter coordinates
volatility_banner <- ggplot(data = cre_projected %>% filter(Volatility > 0)) +
  layer_spatial(london) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(color = Volatility), 
    size = 0.075,
    alpha = 0.9,
    stroke = 0.15
  )+
  scale_color_viridis_c(     # Changed to 'scale_fill' to match the mapping above
    option = "mako",
    name = NULL,
    direction = 1,
    trans = "log10"
  ) +
  # --- THE PANORAMIC ZOOM (Strict 4:1 Ratio in Meters) ---
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(-51000, 29000), 
    ylim = c(6701000, 6721000), 
    expand = FALSE 
  )+
  theme_void() + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",              
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0, "cm")
  )

# 2. Save the perfectly proportioned image
ggsave(
  filename = "linkedin_header_volatility_magma.jpeg", 
  plot = volatility_banner, 
  device = "jpeg",
  width = 1584, 
  height = 396, 
  units = "px",
  dpi = 600
)
```

Descriptive statistics

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(sf)
library(moments) # For skewness and kurtosis
library(knitr)   # For LaTeX table generation

# 1. Calculate the descriptive statistics
summary_stats <- cre_projected %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(Value, Volatility, Liquidity) %>%
  # Pivot the data so variables become rows (perfect for a table)
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(), 
    names_to = "Variable", 
    values_to = "Measurement"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Measurement, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(Measurement, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Std. Dev.` = sd(Measurement, na.rm = TRUE),
    Skewness = skewness(Measurement, na.rm = TRUE),
    Kurtosis = kurtosis(Measurement, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # Force the order to match your thesis layout (Value, Volatility, Liquidity)
  arrange(match(Variable, c("Value", "Volatility", "Liquidity")))

# 2. View the clean dataframe in R
print(summary_stats)

# 3. Generate the raw LaTeX code to copy/paste into your thesis
print(kable(
  summary_stats, 
  format = "latex", 
  booktabs = TRUE, 
  digits = 2, # Rounds to 2 decimal places for clean formatting
  caption = "\\textbf{Descriptive Statistics and Distributional Diagnostics.}"
))
```

morans I\

```{r}
coords <- st_coordinates(cre_projected)
nb_1000 <- dnearneigh(coords, d1 = 0, d2 = 1000)

# Handle the "islands" (properties with zero neighbors) using zero.policy = TRUE
listw_1000 <- nb2listw(nb_1000, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)

# 2. Define a custom function to run the Monte Carlo Moran's I and extract metrics
get_moran_metrics <- function(variable_vector, listw_obj, nsim = 999) {
  
  # Set seed for exact reproducibility in your thesis
  set.seed(42) 
  
  # Run the permutation test
  mc_result <- moran.mc(variable_vector, listw = listw_obj, nsim = nsim, zero.policy = TRUE)
  
  # Extract the observed Moran's I statistic
  moran_i <- mc_result$statistic
  
  # Calculate the empirical Z-score from the permutations
  # (Observed - Mean of Simulations) / Std Dev of Simulations
  simulated_values <- mc_result$res[1:nsim] # Drop the last value which is the observed stat
  z_score <- (moran_i - mean(simulated_values)) / sd(simulated_values)
  
  # Extract the pseudo p-value
  p_val <- mc_result$p.value
  
  # Format p-value for the table (e.g., if it's 0.001, write "< 0.001")
  p_val_formatted <- ifelse(p_val <= 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_val))
  
  return(c(
    `Global Moran's I` = round(moran_i, 4),
    `Z-score` = round(z_score, 2),
    `p-value` = p_val_formatted
  ))
}

# 3. Apply the function to your three variables
variables_to_test <- c("Value", "Volatility", "Liquidity")

# Create an empty list to store the results
moran_results_list <- list()

for (var in variables_to_test) {
  # Drop geometry to pass just the numeric vector
  vec <- cre_multivariate %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% pull(!!sym(var))
  
  # Run the metrics and store
  metrics <- get_moran_metrics(vec, listw_1000)
  moran_results_list[[var]] <- metrics
}

# 4. Bind into a clean dataframe
moran_df <- bind_rows(moran_results_list, .id = "Variable")

# Format the variable names to match the LaTeX math notation
moran_df <- moran_df %>%
  mutate(Variable = case_when(
    Variable == "Value" ~ "Value ($V$)",
    Variable == "Volatility" ~ "Volatility ($\\sigma$)",
    Variable == "Liquidity" ~ "Liquidity ($L$)"
  ))

# 5. Print the results to the R console for your own review
print(moran_df)

# 6. Generate the thesis-ready LaTeX code
kable(
  moran_df, 
  format = "latex", 
  booktabs = TRUE,
  escape = FALSE, # Allows the LaTeX math notation ($V$, $\sigma$) to render properly
  align = c('l', 'c', 'c', 'c'),
  caption = "\\textbf{Global Moran's I Spatial Autocorrelation Diagnostics.} P-values are derived via Monte Carlo permutations ($M=999$) under the null hypothesis of total spatial randomness."
)
```
